detailed_description: The Text to Slug tool turns a title, heading, product name, or short phrase into a simple URL-style slug. It normalizes accents, removes unsupported characters, trims the input, replaces whitespace with your selected separator, and can lowercase the result. The separator control supports hyphen, underscore, or no separator, and the result is shown immediately so you can copy it. The tool is useful for blog drafts, documentation anchors, product handles, static-site routes, and simple file-name ideas. It does not check uniqueness in your CMS, enforce route length, reserve protected words, or provide full transliteration for every script. Review the generated slug before publishing.
usage_steps: Enter the title or phrase you want to slugify.
Choose hyphen, underscore, or no separator.
Leave Lowercase enabled if your URL style uses lowercase slugs.
Review the generated slug shown under the controls.
Copy the slug when it fits your URL style.
Check uniqueness and reserved routes in your CMS or router.
usage_examples: Create a documentation anchor from a section heading.
Draft a product handle for a catalog URL.
Switch the separator to underscore for an internal file-name draft.

faqs.question: Which separators are available?
faqs.answer: You can choose hyphen, underscore, or no separator for whitespace in the source text.

faqs.question: Does it guarantee a unique URL?
faqs.answer: No. You still need to check your CMS or application for duplicate slugs.

faqs.question: Can it transliterate every language?
faqs.answer: No. It normalizes accents and removes unsupported characters, so non-Latin text may require manual review.

faqs.question: Should slugs be short?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Short, descriptive slugs are easier to read and share.

faqs.question: Can I copy the slug?
faqs.answer: Yes. The page includes a copy action for the generated slug.
